term.def: A GPU is a computer chip built to do thousands of calculations at once. It powers most AI tools, from chatbots to image generators.

prompt.prompt: Explain in simple terms how an AI tool could track daily air quality near [office or city] and suggest steps to take when AQI turns poor.

quiz.q: The420.in reports that India plans to develop homegrown GPUs within two years.
quiz.why: This directly restates the headline about India's plan for indigenous GPUs.

quiz.q: The Washington Post reports that investors are dumping AI company stocks after Democrats' election sweep.
quiz.why: This restates the Washington Post headline about investor reaction to the election result.

quiz.q: AI software can run without any physical chips or hardware.
quiz.why: Every AI model needs chips like GPUs to process data and give answers, even after training is done.

quiz.q: GPUs were first designed for rendering video game graphics before AI started using them.
quiz.why: GPUs were built for fast graphics rendering, and their number-crunching power later proved ideal for AI tasks too.

quiz.q: Once an AI model finishes training, it needs no further computing power to answer questions.
quiz.why: Running a trained model, called inference, still needs real computing power every time it responds.
